ReportBuilder.xml_summary: Provides methods intended to fill template with data using LINQ Reporting Engine.

linq_template_analysis.template_syntax: LINQ Reporting Engine uses <<[Expression]>> tags in the DOCX template text. Example: <<[Name]>> in the document body is replaced with data.Name value.
linq_template_analysis.creation_approach: Use DocumentBuilder.Write() to insert literal LINQ tag text into the document. The LINQ Reporting Engine processes these during BuildReport().
linq_template_analysis.risk_note: Medium risk: LLM must emit the exact <<[Name]>> LINQ tag syntax in the template creation code AND pass a matching anonymous object. If the LLM does not know LINQ Reporting Engine syntax, the generated example will compile but produce incorrect output or throw at runtime.

support_types_needed: Aspose.Words.DocumentBuilder (to write LINQ template text into document)
Aspose.Words.LowCode.ReportBuilderOptions (optional — not needed for simplest overload)
Aspose.Words.LowCode.ReportBuilderContext (needed only for Create() factory, not for static BuildReport())
Anonymous object or POCO as data source (e.g. new { Name = "World" })
ReportBuilder.fixture_strategy: programmatic_template_docx_with_linq_tags — Create template DOCX programmatically using DocumentBuilder.Write() to insert LINQ Reporting Engine tag text (<<[Name]>>). Pass matching anonymous object as data parameter.
template_hints_needed: report_builder_template_creation_lines: C# lines to create a template DOCX with LINQ tag <<[Name]>> via DocumentBuilder.Write()
report_builder_data_object: anonymous object with field Name = 'World'
report_builder_linq_syntax_note: LINQ tags use <<[FieldName]>> syntax — must match data object property names exactly

FORBIDDEN: {FieldName} or [FieldName] tag syntax — LINQ Reporting Engine requires <<[FieldName]>> format
FORBIDDEN: IMailMergeDataSource or MERGEFIELD syntax — this is ReportBuilder, not MailMerger

ReportBuilder.output_validator_needed: output_file_exists_and_size_gt_zero; DOCX content check: open with Aspose.Words.Document and verify body text contains merged value (e.g. 'Hello, World!') and does NOT contain '<<' LINQ tag markers
words_yml_changes_needed: Add per_type_constraints.ReportBuilder block with required/forbidden lists
ReportBuilder.fixture_gap_detail: Template DOCX must contain <<[Name]>> LINQ tag syntax. DocumentBuilder.Write() can insert this literally. The LLM must know the LINQ Reporting Engine <<[FieldName]>> syntax — this is the primary risk. Few-shot example or explicit constraint injection strongly recommended.
ReportBuilder.llm_risk_note: Medium risk because LINQ tag syntax <<[Name]>> is non-standard and the LLM may substitute MERGEFIELD syntax, Mustache syntax ({Name}), or other template syntax. Mitigation: explicit per_type_constraints with the exact tag format and a few-shot template creation line in template_hints.
ReportBuilder.next_action: 1. Add ReportBuilder to words.yml allowed_types. 2. Add report_builder_template_creation_lines to words.yml template_hints. 3. Add per_type_constraints.ReportBuilder with LINQ syntax constraint. 4. Run pilot. 5. Validate output DOCX does not contain << markers.

wave3_summary.common_blocker_pattern: All three types were blocked by pilot scope restriction (not_in_allowed_types), not by unresolvable technical blockers. All three can be enabled by updating words.yml.
wave3_summary.enablement_order_rationale: Processor is the simplest (no new template fixture needed, reuses existing programmatic_input pattern). MailMerger requires template with MERGEFIELD (well-understood, low LLM risk). ReportBuilder requires LINQ template (medium LLM risk — must inject exact <<[FieldName]>> syntax).
